notes:
This release brings everything accumulated since 1.70.0. It includes security fixes, so updating is recommended.

Subtitles are noticeably larger, with a proportionally heavier outline. The size was chosen by rendering the same frame at several sizes and comparing them, not by guesswork. Long lines now wrap instead of running off the edge of the frame, and all 13 subtitle templates moved to the same scale — picking one no longer shrinks the text back down.

Which moments become clips has changed on game content: dead frames such as loading screens, menus and lobbies no longer become clips. Talk and IRL streams are unaffected, because their screens are static by nature and the value is in the audio. The detection sensitivity setting (Few / Balanced / Many) now moves the audio threshold as well — it previously changed only chat detection, even though three out of four clips are triggered by audio. "Balanced" now actually ships balanced values; the bundled configuration was set to the "Few" numbers while the label said otherwise.

The platform badge setting is now honoured during production. With it off, the strip is not drawn at all and the space goes to the gameplay instead of leaving a blank band.

Security: the update path is stricter — the verification hash is now required, and downloads must use HTTPS from a recognised domain; previously an empty hash field would skip verification entirely. A processing flaw that could be triggered by the name of a channel being recorded has been closed. YouTube credentials are now encrypted on disk with Windows DPAPI, and existing connections migrate on first launch, so you do not need to reconnect your account. Several request-validation gaps in the local panel were closed as well.

Wording: the end-of-trial text was wrong and is now correct. When the trial ends new clip production stops, and the clips you already made are files on your own computer — we do not store them.
